mainTopic: Redeeming a פטר חמור: the lamb's value, redeeming with money, who owns the redeemed donkey, and tithing the lambs
overview: The amud opens by finishing the חכמים's point: the verse requiring a שקל is only about השג יד. רב נחמן rules like the חכמים, and רב יוסף says even a skinny lamb worth a tiny coin can redeem a פטר חמור. רבי טרפון then gives three levels of giving, and רבא rules that the lamb should be worth a רגיא (three זוזים). The גמרא settles the clash between the two rulings: a רגיא is what we tell someone who asks first, but a cheap lamb still works after the fact. ריש לקיש allows redeeming the donkey with money equal to its value, and רבינא shows that even רבי יהודה agrees, since 'lamb' is only a leniency. Next, the גמרא asks who owns a donkey that an outsider redeemed. It proves from a thief's כפל payment that a פטר חמור is not like הקדש, so the donkey stays with the owner. The amud then explains when the redemption lamb is tithed, and brings רב נחמן's rulings about inheriting donkeys and untithed produce through a grandfather who was a כהן. It ends by starting a new ruling about someone who buys טבל, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The shekel verse is about affordability only
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the verse requiring a שקל was written only about השג יד, a person who vowed but cannot afford the full amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written about a case of what a person can afford.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים are answering the other side's proof. The verse that sets a minimum of a שקל applies only to השג יד, so it does not apply to redeeming a פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other opinion used a verse to say the redemption lamb must be worth at least a שקל. The חכמים limit that verse to its own topic: a poor person who vowed a ערך and can only pay what he can afford. So the שקל minimum does not carry over to the donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: What a person can afford; the rule for a poor person who vowed a ערך
It is written (in the תורה)

phrases.english: It is written regarding affordability.
phrases.notes: This finishes an answer from the page before: the פסוק with the שקל minimum is about someone who vowed a ערך but can't afford it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the previous page's back-and-forth about the source for a שקל minimum.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting a verse to its own context
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse's שקל minimum applies to redeeming a פטר חמור as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שקל minimum applies only to השג יד in ערכין, not to the donkey's redemption.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the הלכה follows the חכמים, so the lamb does not need to be worth a שקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The הלכה follows the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a practical ruling in the argument: we follow the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the discussion, we now know what to actually do. A פטר חמור may be redeemed with a lamb worth less than a שקל.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law we follow
The Sages, the majority opinion
An אמורא who gives the ruling here

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The law is in accordance with the words of the Sages,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the argument that just finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows the חכמים: no שקל minimum for the redemption lamb.

steps.title: How little can the lamb be worth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how low the value of the lamb can go.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much must it be worth?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. Now that there is no שקל minimum, the גמרא asks what the lowest value is, and the next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the שקל minimum leaves an open question. Is there any lower limit at all?

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רב נחמן's ruling by asking about the minimum value.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The lowest value a redemption lamb may have.

steps.title: Even a skinny lamb worth a tiny coin
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that even a thin lamb worth only a דנקא is acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Even a skinny lamb worth only a דנקא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question: even a thin, cheap lamb worth only a tiny coin works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the bar very low. Both the lamb's poor condition and its tiny value are not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A thin, scrawny lamb
A very small coin (a מעה)
Worth (literally 'son of')

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Even a lean lamb worth a danka,
phrases.notes: A דנקא is a very small coin, so this lamb is both skinny and nearly worthless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אֲפִילּוּ פַּטְרוֹזָא בַּר דַּנְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'how much?'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even a lean lamb worth a דנקא is acceptable.

steps.title: רבא finds support in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה already taught this when it said the lamb may be big or small.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We also learned this in the משנה: 'big or small.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up רב יוסף by pointing to the משנה's words 'big or small.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה allows a small lamb, it shows that size and value don't matter. That supports רב יוסף's very low minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a משנה)
Big or small

phrases.english: Rava said:
We too have learned it:
Big or small.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's answer from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's ruling that even a cheap, lean lamb works

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב יוסף needed to say this, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף: if any amount is fine, why say it? The next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים allow a lamb of any value, a lamb worth a דנקא should obviously work. So רב יוסף's statement seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious!

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רב יוסף's statement was needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the lamb may be worth any amount, saying 'even a דנקא' teaches nothing new.

steps.title: First answer: such a low value might be rejected
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought a value this tiny is too little.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: not as little as that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: without רב יוסף, we might think such a tiny value is too little.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Any amount' could be understood as 'less than a שקל, but still something real.' רב יוסף teaches that even a tiny amount counts.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said
So much (here: so little)

phrases.english: You might have said: not that much?
phrases.notes: He means: not that little. One might think so low a value is not enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא (ruling out a possible mistake)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A lamb worth only a דנקא is too cheap to count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a lamb of tiny value works.

steps.title: Second answer: a skinny lamb might be rejected
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, one might think a lean lamb is not fit because of its poor condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else: you might think a skinny lamb doesn't count. So he teaches us it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer: the new point is about the lamb's thinness, not its price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if value doesn't matter, maybe the lamb's poor physical state does. רב יוסף teaches that a scrawny lamb is also fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively
He teaches us (that it is not so)

phrases.english: Alternatively, a lean lamb, not?
He teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation for why רב יוסף's statement was needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A lean lamb is unfit because of its poor condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: A lean lamb is also valid for redemption.
steps.whatToRemember: The lamb for redeeming a פטר חמור can be worth very little, even a דנקא, and it can even be skinny.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה asks רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה had a פטר חמור and asked רבי טרפון how much he must give the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה had a firstborn donkey. He sent it to רבי טרפון and asked: How much do I need to give the כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. רבי יהודה נשיאה asks a practical question about redeeming his firstborn donkey, setting up רבי טרפון's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned the lamb can be worth very little. Now we see a real case asking what amount a person should actually give.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb
He sent it
To give to the כהן

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia had a firstborn donkey,
he sent it before Rabbi Tarfon,
he said to him:
How much do I need to give to a priest?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rule to a real-life story about the amount to give.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much the lamb given to the כהן should be worth.

steps.title: רבי טרפון's three levels of giving
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון answers that a generous person gives a סלע, a stingy person a שקל, and an in-between person a רגיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't they say: a generous person gives a סלע, a stingy person a שקל, and an in-between person a רגיא?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון answers with a known teaching: how much you give depends on how generous you are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is about what is fitting to give, not the bare legal minimum, which we already saw can be tiny. The three levels depend on the giver's attitude.

keyTerms.meaning: A generous person (literally 'a good eye')
A stingy person (literally 'a bad eye')
A coin worth more than a שקל
A coin worth an in-between amount

steps.confusionAlert: This may look like it clashes with רב יוסף's tiny minimum. The גמרא raises exactly that problem in step 14 and solves it in step 15.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי טרפון answering.

phrases.english: Didn't they say:
A generous eye, with a sela,
a miserly eye, with a shekel,
an intermediate one, with a ragya.
phrases.notes: A רגיא is a coin between the other two in value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה נשיאה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Generous: a סלע; stingy: a שקל; in-between: a רגיא.

steps.title: רבא rules the lamb should be worth a רגיא
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows the middle amount, the רגיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is like the רגיא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles which of רבי טרפון's three amounts is the practical הלכה: the in-between one, the רגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, רבי טרפון gave three amounts depending on how generous a person is. רבא now picks one as the standard: the middle amount. So the lamb given to the כהן should be worth a רגיא.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law; how we actually rule
A middle coin value, between a סלע and a שקל

phrases.english: Rava said:
The halakha is like the ragya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks the practical ruling from רבי טרפון's three options.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lamb for redeeming a פטר חמור should be worth a רגיא.

steps.title: How much is a רגיא worth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the value of a רגיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: what is a רגיא actually worth?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא used the word רגיא without giving a number. Before the ruling can be used, we need to know the amount.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the term רבא just used.

steps.title: A רגיא is three זוזים, close to both sides
steps.stepSummary: A רגיא is three זוזים, and its name comes from being close to both the higher and lower amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three זוזים. It is close to here and close to here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a רגיא is three זוזים, and explains the name with a play on words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סלע is four זוזים and a שקל is two. Three sits right between them, so it is 'רגיל' (close) to each side, which is where the name רגיא comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: זוזים (דינרים), basic silver coins
Close to, near (a play on the word רגיא)

phrases.english: Three zuz.
phrases.notes: A סלע is four זוזים and a שקל is two, so three is right in the middle.

phrases.english: It is close to here and close to there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A רגיא equals three זוזים, between a סלע (four) and a שקל (two).

steps.title: Two rulings seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבא's ruling clashes with the earlier ruling that a lamb of any small value is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: one הלכתא against another הלכתא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: we now have two official rulings that seem to disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier רב נחמן ruled that the הלכה follows the חכמים (step 2), and רב יוסף explained that even a lamb worth a דנקא is enough (step 4). Now רבא says the lamb should be worth three זוזים. Both are stated as הלכה, so how can both be true?

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty; this is a problem
One ruling against another ruling

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: halakha against halakha!
phrases.notes: The other ruling is רב נחמן's: the הלכה follows the חכמים, so even a lamb worth very little works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רבא's ruling against the earlier accepted ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the lamb must be worth a רגיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier ruling allowed a lamb of any small value, so requiring three זוזים contradicts it.

steps.title: One ruling is advice beforehand, the other is after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רבא's rule is for someone who asks first; the earlier rule is for someone who already redeemed on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: here, it is about someone who comes to ask; there, it is about someone who acts on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the clash by applying each ruling to a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person comes to ask what to do, we tell him to give a lamb worth three זוזים. But if he already redeemed with a cheaper lamb without asking, it still counts. So both rulings are true, just for different moments.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes to ask for guidance before acting
Acts on his own, without asking

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a cheap lamb is wrong. It works after the fact; three זוזים is just what we tell someone who asks first.
steps.whatToRemember: Ask first: give a lamb worth a רגיא (three זוזים). Already done with a cheaper lamb: it still counts.

phrases.english: It is not difficult,
here, it is about one who comes to consult,
phrases.notes: This is רבא's three-זוזים ruling.

phrases.english: there, it is about one who acts on his own.
phrases.notes: This is the earlier ruling: if he already did it, even a cheap lamb works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: before acting vs. after acting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two rulings disagree about the minimum value of the lamb.
steps.terutzMaskana: A רגיא is the advice for one who asks; any small value works for one who already acted.

steps.title: No lamb? Redeem the donkey with its value in money
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that someone without a lamb may redeem the פטר חמור with money equal to the donkey's worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said in the name of ריש לקיש: Someone who has a פטר חמור but no lamb to redeem it with may redeem it with its value.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: what to do when there is no lamb available for the redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a פטר חמור is redeemed with a lamb. ריש לקיש says that if you have no lamb, you may give the כהן money equal to the donkey's value instead. This raises the question of whether a lamb is really required.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn donkey, which must be redeemed
To redeem it
With its value (in money)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said that Reish Lakish said:
One who has a firstborn donkey
but does not have a lamb to redeem it with,
may redeem it with its value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: redeeming without a lamb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without a lamb, one may redeem the פטר חמור with money equal to the donkey's value.

steps.title: Whose opinion does ריש לקיש follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא ריש לקיש's ruling fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier opinion this ruling is based on. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an earlier argument (on ט.) about whether a lamb is strictly required. The גמרא wants to see which side ריש לקיש's ruling belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source opinion behind step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view ריש לקיש's ruling follows.

steps.title: It cannot follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ruling cannot match רבי יהודה, since he holds the תורה insists on a lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it follows רבי יהודה, but he said: The תורה was particular that it be with a lamb!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one option, רבי יהודה, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds the תורה specifically wants a lamb for this redemption. So he would not allow money instead. That rules him out as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would say
The תורה was particular about it
A lamb (or kid)

phrases.english: If you say it follows Rabbi Yehuda,
but he said:
The Torah was particular about it, with a lamb!
phrases.notes: This refers back to רבי יהודה's view on ט., that only a lamb works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the first possible answer to step 17 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that ריש לקיש follows רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה requires a lamb specifically, so money would not work for him.

steps.title: It follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The ruling must follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that ריש לקיש's ruling matches רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה is ruled out, the other side, רבי שמעון, must be the source. He does not insist on a lamb, so money equal to the donkey's value works.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the correct answer)

phrases.english: Rather, it follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer after rejecting רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש's ruling follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב אחא teaches it this way
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא teaches that ריש לקיש's ruling follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא taught it this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רב אחא taught the discussion this way. This sets up רבינא's problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא's version connects ריש לקיש's ruling to רבי שמעון. This matters because it raises the question of whether we actually rule that way.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way

phrases.english: Rav Acha teaches it this way,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names who teaches the conclusion of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אחא teaches that ריש לקיש follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבינא: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא is bothered: in disputes between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא found it difficult: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the הלכה is like רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the conclusion: if the ruling follows רבי שמעון, it goes against the usual rule of whom we follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that when רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. So how could ריש לקיש give a practical ruling that follows רבי שמעון?

keyTerms.meaning: It was difficult for him
The law follows רבי יהודה

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge decides whether one may really redeem a פטר חמור with money, or must find a lamb.

phrases.english: Ravina found it difficult:
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon,
the halakha is like Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion that ריש לקיש follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling, now tied to רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון, so a ruling based on רבי שמעון seems against the הלכה.

steps.title: An unattributed משנה follows רבי יהודה, so how can the הלכה follow רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא adds force to his challenge: the anonymous משנה about a doubtful פטר חמור follows רבי יהודה, so ruling like רבי שמעון seems wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And besides, the תנא taught us an anonymous משנה that follows רבי יהודה, and you say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא is finishing his complaint from the last step. He adds a second reason why the הלכה should not follow רבי שמעון here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two reasons to rule like רבי יהודה. First, there is the general rule that in disputes between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. Second, a סתם משנה (an anonymous משנה) on this exact topic matches his view. So placing ריש לקיש's ruling only in רבי שמעון's camp makes it look like a ruling we don't follow.

keyTerms.meaning: An anonymous, unattributed teaching; a סתם משנה usually signals the accepted הלכה
The teacher or author of the משנה
'And you say...?!', a phrase showing surprise at a contradiction

phrases.english: And the tanna taught us an unattributed teaching in line with Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about a donkey that may or may not be a firstborn. The גמרא showed earlier that it matches רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: and you say the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon?!

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Continuation of the קשיא in step 21
steps.triggerLanguage: וּסְתַם לַן תַּנָּא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רבינא's challenge from step 21 with a second argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא's claim that ריש לקיש's ruling follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both the general rule of who wins in their disputes and an anonymous משנה point to ruling like רבי יהודה. So a ruling that only works for רבי שמעון would not be practical הלכה.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה agrees, because a firstborn donkey is no stricter than consecrated property
steps.stepSummary: רבינא concludes that ריש לקיש's ruling fits רבי יהודה too. A פטר חמור should not be stricter than הקדש, and 'with a lamb' was said only as a leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you can even say this follows רבי יהודה. A פטר חמור should not be stricter than הקדש. The תורה did not say 'with a lamb' to make it harder for the owner, only to make it easier for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives up the idea that the ruling depends on רבי שמעון. He shows that even רבי יהודה would allow redeeming the donkey with something worth its full value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הקדש can be redeemed with any item worth its value, so a פטר חמור surely can too. The word 'lamb' in the Torah is a leniency: a lamb is cheaper than a donkey. It is not a strict requirement that rules out other payment. This removes the problem from the last step, because now the ruling fits the view we actually follow.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Even if you say...', which shows the ruling works even for the other opinion
Consecrated property belonging to the Temple
To be strict
To be lenient
A lamb or kid; the Torah's stated payment for redeeming a פטר חמור

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the lamb is the only option for רבי יהודה. Even by his view, the lamb is a cheaper option the תורה gave as a favor. Redeeming with something worth the donkey's full value also works.
steps.whyThisMatters: It lets ריש לקיש's ruling stand as practical הלכה without going against the rule that we follow רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rather, even if you say it follows Rabbi Yehuda,
it should not be stricter than consecrated property,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the firstborn donkey. הקדש can be redeemed with anything worth its value.

phrases.english: and the Torah did not say 'with a lamb'
to be strict with him, but rather to be lenient with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge by removing the need to tie the ruling to רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the ruling fits both opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יהודה insists only a lamb works, so ריש לקיש's ruling had to follow רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי יהודה agrees that redeeming with full value works, because 'lamb' was only a leniency and הקדש is redeemed this way.

steps.title: רב נחמן redeemed a donkey with boiled vegetables
steps.stepSummary: A story shows the ruling being used in practice: רב נחמן בריה דרב יוסף redeemed a פטר חמור with boiled vegetables worth its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן the son of רב יוסף redeemed a firstborn donkey with boiled vegetables worth its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a real case that matches what was just said. Someone actually redeemed a donkey with ordinary items worth its full value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the ruling was practical הלכה, not just theory. Even cheap, everyday food counts, as long as its total value equals the donkey's value.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeemed
Boiled vegetables
At its value, worth as much as the donkey

steps.whatToRemember: A פטר חמור can be redeemed with a lamb or with anything worth the donkey's value. This works even according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman son of Rav Yosef
redeemed it with boiled vegetables worth its value.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף פָּרֵיק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case that supports the conclusion of step 23.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a פטר חמור may be redeemed with anything worth its value
steps.raayaSupportSource: What רב נחמן בריה דרב יוסף actually did

steps.title: Redeeming someone else's firstborn donkey works
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: רב שיזבי quotes רב הונא that if you redeem another person's פטר חמור, the redemption takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said in the name of רב הונא: someone who redeems his friend's firstborn donkey, the donkey is redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings a ruling that an outsider can redeem someone else's firstborn donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the owner did not do the redemption, the donkey still becomes redeemed. This sets up the next question: after such a redemption, who owns the donkey?

keyTerms.meaning: One who redeems
A firstborn donkey, which must be redeemed
What he redeemed is redeemed; the redemption works

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Sheizevi said in the name of Rav Huna:
one who redeems the firstborn donkey of his friend,
what he redeemed is redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, unrelated to the previous challenge-and-answer exchange.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Redeeming another person's פטר חמור is valid.

steps.title: Who owns the redeemed donkey, the redeemer or the owner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a question: after an outsider redeems the donkey, does it belong to him or to the original owner?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: does the redeemed donkey belong to the one who redeemed it, or perhaps to the owner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds on רב הונא's ruling. It asks a follow-up question about who ends up owning the donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the redemption works. What we don't know is whether paying for it makes the outsider the new owner, or whether the original owner keeps the donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them, an open question
Or perhaps
The owner

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
does what he redeemed belong to the redeemer,
or perhaps what he redeemed belongs to the owner?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question built on רב הונא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the redeemed donkey becomes the redeemer's property or stays with the original owner.

steps.title: The question only arises according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the question. According to רבי שמעון the donkey clearly belongs to the owner. The doubt only exists according to רבי יהודה, who forbids benefit before redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון, there is no question: since he says you may benefit from the donkey, it is the owner's property. The question is according to רבי יהודה, who says benefit is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers part of the question by saying when it does and doesn't apply. This sets up the real question, which is according to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the owner may use the donkey even before redemption, so it is clearly his property. An outsider's payment doesn't change that. For רבי יהודה, the unredeemed donkey is forbidden, so it isn't really usable property yet. Maybe the one whose payment makes it permitted is the one who gets it.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
You should not ask the question here; it is clear
Permitted to benefit from
Forbidden to benefit from
Property, money

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, you should not ask,
since he says it is permitted for benefit,
it is the owner's property,
where you should ask is according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who says it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from step 26 to apply only according to רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי שמעון, the donkey belongs to the owner. The question applies only according to רבי יהודה, and steps 29-31 answer it.

steps.title: The two sides of the question: like consecrated property or not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both sides of its doubt. Maybe a פטר חמור is like הקדש, where whoever pays the redemption money acquires the item. Or maybe it is different, because the owner keeps a share in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we compare it to הקדש, where the Torah says 'he gives the money and it becomes his'? Or perhaps, since the owner owns the in-between value, it is not like הקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes asking its question from Step 26. It shows the reasoning behind each possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: with הקדש, whoever pays the redemption money gets the item, so the outsider who redeemed should keep the donkey. Side two: the owner may redeem with a lamb worth less than the donkey, so the difference in value is really his. That means the donkey was never fully 'holy' like הקדש, and it should go back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: compare it to; treat it as similar to
'He gives the money and it is his': the פסוק about redeeming הקדש
or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
the in-between; the difference in value

steps.confusionAlert: Remember, this whole question only works according to רבי יהודה (Step 27). רבי שמעון already holds the donkey is the owner's.

phrases.english: Do we compare it to consecrated property,
and the Merciful One said:
"And he will give the money and it will be his"
phrases.notes: This פסוק is about redeeming הקדש. Whoever pays the money gets the item, even someone who didn't consecrate it.

phrases.english: or perhaps, since he owns them
in the in-between,
phrases.notes: He means the gap in value. The owner can redeem with a lamb worth less than the donkey, so that extra value is his.

phrases.english: it is not similar to consecrated property?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the doubt that Step 27 limited to רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a פטר חמור compared to הקדש, so the outsider who redeemed it acquires it? Or does the owner's share in the value make it different, so it returns to the owner?

steps.title: A thief who steals a firstborn donkey pays double
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן brings a ברייתא: someone who steals another person's פטר חמור pays כפל to the owner. Even though the owner can't use it now, he will be able to later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Come and hear. One who steals his friend's פטר חמור pays double to the owner. Even though the owner doesn't have it now, he will have it afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a source to answer the question. This step quotes the source, and the next steps explain how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new piece of information is that stealing a פטר חמור brings the penalty of כפל, paid to the owner. The ברייתא adds that the owner's rights count even though he can only use the donkey after it is redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (introduces a source as proof)
one who steals
double payment, the penalty a thief pays
afterward; later on

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: Come and hear:
One who steals the firstborn donkey of his fellow
pays the double payment to the owner,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עַכְשָׁיו —
phrases.english: and even though he does not have it now,
he has it afterward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to settle the question asked in Step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That a פטר חמור is not like הקדש, so after an outsider redeems it, it belongs to the original owner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: one who steals a פטר חמור pays כפל to the owner.

steps.title: The ברייתא must follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the ברייתא follows. It cannot be רבי שמעון, because he allows using the donkey right away. So it must be רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי שמעון, why does the owner 'not have it now'? Rather, it is obviously רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down which תנא the ברייתא follows. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'he doesn't have it now' only make sense if using the donkey is forbidden before redemption. That is רבי יהודה's view. This matters because the question was only asked according to רבי יהודה (Step 27), so the ברייתא can now answer it.

keyTerms.meaning: whose view is this?
if you say
why?
it is obvious

phrases.english: Whose view is it? If we say Rabbi Shimon,
why does he not have it now?
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון lets the owner benefit from the donkey even before redemption, so he would 'have it' already.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obviously Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the ברייתא from Step 29, so it can be used for רבי יהודה's version of the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא does the ברייתא follow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה, since only he says the owner can't use the donkey before it is redeemed.

steps.title: No double payment for consecrated property, so the donkey is not like it
steps.stepSummary: If a פטר חמור were like הקדש, a thief would not pay כפל, since the Torah says כפל applies to stealing 'from a man's house', not from הקדש. Since the ברייתא says he does pay כפל, a פטר חמור is not like הקדש. The proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think we compare it to הקדש, the Torah said 'and it is stolen from the man's house', and not from the house of הקדש! There is nothing more to say.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof and declares it airtight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stealing הקדש carries no כפל. Even according to רבי יהודה, the ברייתא makes a thief pay כפל for a פטר חמור. So a פטר חמור does not have the status of הקדש. That means the outsider does not acquire it by redeeming it, and it stays with the original owner.

keyTerms.meaning: and if it enters your mind (if you were to think)
'and it is stolen from the man's house': the source for כפל
and nothing more; the proof is complete

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה too, a פטר חמור is not like הקדש, because a thief pays כפל for it. So if an outsider redeems someone else's פטר חמור, the donkey still belongs to the original owner.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the question from Step 26 for both תנאים. With רבי שמעון it was clear already, and now it is proven for רבי יהודה too.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that we compare it to consecrated property,
the Merciful One said: "And it be stolen from the man's house",
phrases.notes: This פסוק is where the Torah tells us a thief pays double.

phrases.english: and not from the house of the Temple!
phrases.notes: So someone who steals הקדש does not pay double. If the donkey were like הקדש, the ברייתא couldn't require double.

phrases.english: And nothing more.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לְהֶקְדֵּשׁ מְדַמֵּינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא, now shown to follow רבי יהודה, to complete the proof that a פטר חמור is not like הקדש.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A פטר חמור is not compared to הקדש, even according to רבי יהודה. If an outsider redeems it, it belongs to the original owner.

steps.title: When does the redemption lamb get tithed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the two donkeys. A ברייתא asks in what case the משנה's lamb goes into the pen to be tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one donkey had given birth before and one had not. The Rabbis taught: in what case did they say the lamb enters the pen to be tithed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that asks a question about it. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the lamb set aside because of the doubt is tithed with the owner's other animals. The ברייתא is puzzled by this. Whose lamb is it, and how can it be tithed? It wants the exact case where this rule works.

keyTerms.meaning: She has already given birth before. So her next baby is not a firstborn.
The Rabbis taught. This opens a ברייתא.
A pen for animals. The animals are counted there for tithing.
To be tithed. Here it means מעשר בהמה, one out of every ten animals.

phrases.english: One had given birth before and one had not given birth before, etc.
phrases.notes: We're back in the משנה: two donkeys, and we don't know which one had the male. [כו׳] just means "and so on".

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
In what case did they say
that it enters the pen to be tithed?
phrases.notes: "It" is the lamb that was set aside because of the doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The גמרא moves from stealing a פטר חמור back to another line in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what exact case can the lamb used to redeem a doubtful firstborn donkey be tithed?

steps.title: It cannot be a lamb the priest received
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules out the case where the lamb was already given to a כהן. A gift is exempt from מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say it means after the lamb came into a כהן's hands. We learned: an animal that was bought, or was given as a gift, is exempt from animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes away one possible case before giving its real answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simplest guess is that the כהן received the lamb and then tithes it with his flock. But a כהן gets the lamb as a gift. A משנה teaches that bought or gifted animals are exempt from מעשר בהמה. So this cannot be the case the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot say. Used to rule out an option.
For we have learned. It brings a proof from a משנה.
An animal that was bought.
A gift.
The tithe of animals. Every tenth animal is holy.

phrases.english: You cannot say
that it is where it came into the hand of a priest,
for we learned:
one that was bought, or that was given to him as a gift,
is exempt from animal tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It starts answering the question in step 32 by ruling out one case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the idea that the משנה means a lamb already given to the כהן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A gift is exempt from מעשר בהמה. A כהן's lamb is a gift, so he could not tithe it.

steps.title: An Israelite with ten doubtful firstborn donkeys
steps.stepSummary: The case is an Israelite who has ten doubtful firstborn donkeys. He sets aside ten lambs, tithes them, and keeps them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means an Israelite who had ten doubtful firstborn donkeys in his house. He sets aside ten lambs for them, tithes them, and they are his.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its real answer. The lambs stay with the Israelite owner, and he is the one who tithes them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each donkey is only a doubtful firstborn. So the כהן cannot prove any lamb belongs to him, and the lambs stay with the owner. Because they are his own animals and not a gift, they are counted for מעשר בהמה. With ten lambs there is a full group of ten to tithe.

keyTerms.meaning: Donkeys that may or may not be firstborn.
He sets aside.
Lambs or kids (plural of שה). They are used to redeem a פטר חמור.
And they are his. The owner keeps the lambs.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's tithed lamb belongs to an Israelite. It is a redemption lamb for a doubtful firstborn, which he keeps because no כהן can prove a claim to it.

phrases.english: Rather, it is with an Israelite
who had ten
uncertain firstborn donkeys in his house,
who sets aside ten lambs for them,
and he tithes them, and they are his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 33 ruled out the כהן case. Here the ברייתא gives the case that works.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An Israelite with ten doubtful firstborn donkeys sets aside ten lambs. He keeps them and tithes them.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this ברייתא supports the same ruling that רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב נחמן. רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: an Israelite who had ten doubtful firstborn donkeys sets aside ten lambs for them, tithes them, and they are his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא matches a ruling of an אמורא, so the ruling now has backing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן gave the exact same law in the name of his teacher. The ברייתא, which is an older source, says the same thing word for word. So his ruling is confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports him. A source backs up someone's ruling.
An אמורא, the teacher רב נחמן quotes here.
And he tithes them.

phrases.english: This supports Rav Nachman,
for Rav Nachman said
that Rabbah bar Avuh said:
An Israelite who had
ten uncertain firstborn donkeys
sets aside ten lambs for them,
and tithes them, and they are his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It links the ברייתא's answer in step 34 to רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling in the name of רבה בר אבוה about ten doubtful firstborn donkeys.

steps.title: Ten definite firstborn donkeys passed down through the family
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן brings another ruling from רבה בר אבוה. It is about an Israelite who inherited ten definite firstborn donkeys from his grandfather, a כהן. That כהן had inherited them from his own grandfather, an Israelite. The ruling itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: an Israelite had ten definite firstborn donkeys in his house. They came to him from his mother's father, a כהן. That כהן had received them from his own mother's father, an Israelite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second ruling of רב נחמן and lays out a detailed case. This step only sets up the case; the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the donkeys are definitely firstborn, not doubtful. They started with an Israelite, so they needed redemption. Then they passed to a כהן, and then to an Israelite grandson. The גמרא is building the facts so it can ask what the grandson must do.

keyTerms.meaning: Definite. Here: surely firstborn.
They fell to him, meaning he got them by inheritance.
His mother's father, his grandfather on his mother's side.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the earlier case. There the donkeys were only maybe firstborn. Here they are surely firstborn, and the twist is how they were passed down the family.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said
that Rabbah bar Avuh said:
An Israelite who had

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂרָה פִּטְרֵי חֲמוֹרִים וַדָּאִין בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: ten definite firstborn donkeys in his house,
that came to him from the estate of his mother's father, a priest,
and that mother's father, the priest,

steps.title: The grandson redeems the donkeys and keeps the lambs
steps.stepSummary: This completes the ruling begun in step 36. The Israelite grandson sets aside ten lambs for the ten firstborn donkeys, tithes them, and they belong to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sets aside ten lambs for them, tithes them, and they are his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the ruling for the case set up in the last step. The grandson redeems the donkeys with lambs and keeps the lambs for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the lambs that redeem a פטר חמור go to a כהן. Here the donkeys passed through a grandfather who was a כהן, and that כהן was entitled to those gifts. So the grandson inherits that right and keeps the lambs, as if his grandfather had set them aside and left them to him. Since the lambs are now his own, he must also put them through מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: sets aside, designates
lambs (used to redeem a firstborn donkey)
he tithes them (here, through מעשר בהמה)
and they belong to him

phrases.english: He sets aside ten lambs for them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the ten definite firstborn donkeys from step 36.

phrases.english: and tithes them, and they are his.
phrases.notes: Because the lambs stay with him, they go into the pen for מעשר בהמה, as in step 34.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ruling for the case that step 36 set up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An Israelite who inherited definite firstborn donkeys through a grandfather who was a כהן redeems them with ten lambs, tithes the lambs, and keeps them.

steps.title: The same rule for inherited untithed produce
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רבה בר אבוה again. An Israelite has smoothed piles of untithed produce that reached him through a grandfather who was a כהן. That כהן got it from his own grandfather, an Israelite. The grandson tithes the produce and keeps the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: An Israelite has smoothed piles of untithed produce in his house. It came to him from the house of his mother's father, a כהן. That grandfather, the כהן, got it from the house of his own mother's father, an Israelite. The grandson tithes the produce, and the gifts are his.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a second ruling that matches the donkey case, this time about produce. The family chain is the same, and so is the result: the Israelite grandson keeps the gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smoothed piles are fully processed, so the gifts for כהנים and לויים are already owed. The produce passed through a כהן who was entitled to those gifts. So his Israelite grandson separates them and keeps them, just as with the lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: untithed produce, from which gifts have not yet been separated
smoothed piles; the final stage of processing grain, which makes it owe tithes
his mother's father (maternal grandfather)
fell to him, meaning he inherited it

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:

phrases.aramaic: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ טְבָלִים מְמוֹרָחִין בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: An Israelite who had smoothed piles of untithed produce in his house,
phrases.notes: Smoothing the pile is the last step of processing, so now the produce must be tithed.

phrases.english: which he inherited from the house of his mother's father, a priest,
and that mother's father, the priest,

phrases.aramaic: נָפְלוּ לוֹ מִבֵּית אֲבִי אִמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: had inherited it from the house of his own mother's father, an Israelite —
phrases.notes: This is the same family chain as the donkey case in step 36.

phrases.english: he tithes it, and they are his.
phrases.notes: "They" means the gifts he separates. He keeps them, as if his grandfather the כהן had left them to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel ruling from the same teachers, applied to produce instead of donkeys.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An Israelite who inherited untithed produce through a grandfather who was a כהן separates the gifts and keeps them.

steps.title: Why the donkey ruling alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both rulings are needed. The donkey case does not teach the produce case. With produce, one might say that gifts never separated are treated as if never separated, so the grandson would not keep them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If he had taught us only the first case, we would say it works there because it stands as already separated. But here, gifts that were not separated are treated as if they were not separated, so I might say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב נחמן needed to say both rulings. This part shows why the donkey ruling could not teach us the produce ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the donkey case, the lambs count as standing separated, so it is easy to see the כהן grandfather as already owning them. With produce, the gifts must actually be separated to exist as gifts. Since the כהן never separated them, maybe he never owned them, and his Israelite grandson would not keep them. That is why we need the second ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: and it is necessary, meaning both statements are needed
he taught us
the first one (the donkey case)
priestly gifts that were not yet separated
I might say no (the rule does not apply)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to רב נחמן. A צריכותא just explains why each ruling teaches something the other could not.
steps.whatToRemember: Both rulings say the grandson keeps the gifts. The produce ruling adds that this is true even though the gifts were never separated.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if he had taught us only the first —
phrases.notes: "The first" is the firstborn donkey case.

phrases.english: that is because it stands already separated.
But here —
phrases.notes: "Here" means the untithed produce case.

phrases.english: gifts that were not separated
are treated as if they were not separated,
I might say no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the second ruling (step 38) is needed beside the first (steps 36-37).
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: explains why each of two similar rulings is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the produce ruling, one might think gifts never separated stay unowned by the כהן, so his Israelite grandson could not keep them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even gifts never separated count as belonging to the כהן grandfather, so the Israelite grandson keeps them.

steps.title: Why the produce ruling cannot teach the donkey ruling
steps.stepSummary: Finishing the צריכא: had רב נחמן taught only the produce case, we might think the donkey case is different, since a lamb must be brought from elsewhere. So both rulings are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if רב נחמן had taught us only the produce case, I would say the grandson keeps the gifts there because the gifts can be separated from the produce itself, which is right there. But with the donkeys, a lamb has to be brought from somewhere else, so I would not say the lamb counts as already set aside. That is why both rulings are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why רב נחמן needed both rulings. This time it shows that the produce case could not have taught us the donkey case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With produce, the gifts sit inside the produce itself, so it is easy to treat them as if the כהן grandfather already separated them. With a firstborn donkey, the lamb that redeems it comes from outside, so we might have thought it cannot count as already set aside. Each case has its own reason to doubt, so each ruling teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: And if he had taught us only this case
From itself and within itself

It stands as already separated
It is needed, meaning both statements are necessary

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the cases straight: in both halves, 'here' (הָכָא) means the untithed produce. In this step, 'there' (הָתָם) means the firstborn donkeys.
steps.whatToRemember: Both rulings are needed. Produce has the 'gifts not separated count as not separated' doubt. Donkeys have the 'lamb comes from elsewhere' doubt.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only here,

phrases.notes: 'There' means the firstborn donkeys, which are redeemed with a lamb.

phrases.notes: He means the idea that the gift counts as if the כהן grandfather already set it aside.

steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each of two rulings teaches something the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the produce case alone, one might think the donkey case differs, because the lamb comes from elsewhere and cannot count as already separated.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both rulings are needed. In both cases the grandson keeps the gifts.

steps.title: A new ruling about someone who buys untithed produce
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נתן, quoting רבי חנינא, opens a ruling about a person who buys טבל. The ruling continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נתן said in the name of רבי חנינא: someone who buys untithed produce...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new statement about someone who buys untithed produce. This line only sets up the case, and the ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the produce reached the person by inheritance through a כהן grandfather. Now the produce is bought. The question will be what happens to the gifts in a purchase.
